ACE CREATIVE LEADERSHIP WORKSHOP · LEVEL 2: FORGER

LEVEL 2 工作坊日期｜2026 年 8 月 11 日

把創新構想發展成具體的 MVP 概念。

Level 2 將延續各組在 Level 1 為所選品牌發展的創新構想。透過一日實作，團隊會釐清主要目標客群與核心問題、整理使用者行為資料、形成一套完整的 MVP 概念，並以模擬官方網站呈現。

了解 Level 2 怎麼進行 查看當日流程 ↓
2026 年 8 月 11 日・星期二上午 9:30–下午 5:30台北

教練的話

Chris 與 Joshua 寫給大家的一封信

各位好朋友，

讓我們一起回顧 2026 年 4 月 14 日完成的 Applied Creativity Engine Creative Leadership Workshop Level 1: Explorer。

在這次 workshop 中，我們一起學習了創新與創意的一個核心概念：

Creativity is Remix.

創意不一定是從零開始，而是重新理解一個品牌已經擁有的能力，再將這些能力與新的產業、情境與使用者需求重新組合。

六個團隊各自選擇了一個知名品牌，先從 Technology、Design、Business Model、Customer Engagement 與 Ecosystem 五個面向，探索品牌的 core skills，再進一步研究品牌的 personality、belief 與 leadership direction，萃取出品牌獨特的 DNA。

接著，大家運用 SCAMPER，並與 AI 協作，將品牌的核心能力與不同產業進行 crossover，快速產生大量 innovative ideas。經過團隊討論、判斷與 synthesis，每一組最後都收斂出一個符合品牌 DNA、具有創意，也值得繼續發展的 idea。

六個團隊的成果包括：

  1. Team 1 將 On 延伸為結合精品設計、運動機能與會員服務的私享運動沙龍。
  2. Team 2 將 Picky 轉化為極端環境中的營養與生存方案。
  3. Team 3 結合 Nike 穩定鞋、步態數據與遊戲化會員任務，幫助使用者走得更穩、動得更好。
  4. Team 4 創造了 MUJI 無印寺，透過減少選擇與干擾，幫助人回到剛剛好的生活狀態。
  5. Team 5 將 In-N-Out 的簡單、高品質與隱藏菜單文化，延伸成極簡咖啡館。
  6. Team 6 創造 Alive with Patagonia，讓服飾成為記錄運動、冒險與人生故事的長期載體。

最後，各組也將 idea 整理成 Innovative Idea Summary，並以第一人稱視角創造 user journey，讓原本抽象的概念，開始成為一個可以被理解與想像的產品故事。

這就是 Level 1: Explorer 的成果：

From No Idea to an Innovative Idea.

接下來，在 2026 年 8 月 11 日，我們將一起進入 Level 2: Forger。

在 Forger 中，coaches 將帶領各團隊運用 Human-Centered Design、Design Sprint 與 AI，加速把目前的 innovative idea，逐步鍛造成一個更具體、可被討論、可被驗證的 Minimal Viable Product Concept。

每個團隊也將完成一個 mock official website，以產品已經正式上市的方式，清楚呈現它的目標使用者、核心問題、價值主張、主要功能與使用體驗。

Explorer 幫助我們找到新的可能性。

Forger 將幫助我們把可能性鍛造成一個真正看得見的產品概念。

期待 8 月 11 日與大家再次一起出發。

Chris and Joshua

工作坊當日流程

三個主要工作重點。

01
上午 · 上午 9:30–中午 12:00

聚焦創新構想

重新檢視 Level 1 的構想，選定主要目標客群、釐清核心問題，並完成第一次有意識的調整。

產出：第一次調整後的 Innovative Idea Summary
+
9:30

開場與 Level 1 回顧

確認 Level 2 的目標，快速回顧各組的 Version 1 構想。

9:45

主要目標客群

盤點可能客群，並選定主要目標客群。

10:40

核心問題與 HMW

釐清重要需求，建立主要 How Might We 問題敘述。

11:20

第一次調整

依主要目標客群與核心問題，更新產品構想方向。

02
下午・第一階段 · 下午 1:15–3:15

從使用者證據形成 MVP

從使用者行為出發，依序整理同理心地圖、洞察、機會領域，最後形成最小完整的功能組合。

產出：第二次調整後的 MVP Concept Summary
+
1:15

Empathize 同理

檢視模擬行為資料，建立「說／做／想／感受」同理心地圖。

1:45

Analyze 分析

找出洞察、痛點與期待、資料中的矛盾，以及機會領域。

Refine 精煉

第二次調整

下午・第二階段 · 下午 3:30–5:30

讓概念具體呈現

產出：MVP 概念的模擬官方網站

3:30

LEVEL 2 重點

從構想到 MVP。

這一天的重點不是產生更多點子，而是把團隊已經發展出的品牌創新構想，做得更聚焦、更貼近使用者，也更具體到可以拿來討論與測試。

01Level 1 的起點

為所選品牌發展的創新構想

團隊的 Innovative Idea Summary，包含初步目標客群、假設需求、產品構想與使用者旅程。

這是起始假設，不是不能更改的答案。
02工作坊的進行方式

一套聚焦、以人為本的設計流程

透過 DEAR 流程定義問題、理解行為、整理洞察，並做出清楚的 MVP 產品決策。

快速實作、團隊協作，並搭配 AI 工具。
03Level 2 的產出

一套具體的 MVP 概念

完成主要目標客群、需求依據、核心功能、使用者旅程與模擬官方網站。

能夠用來說明、檢視，並安排下一步驗證。

ACE 獨創的 DEAR 流程

DEAR 是由 Applied Creativity Engine 獨創的工作流程，融合以人為本設計（Human-Centered Design）與 Design Sprint 的核心做法。透過四個相互連結的步驟，協助團隊把初步構想發展成有使用者依據的 MVP。

D Define 定義聚焦目標客群與核心問題 我們要為誰，解決什麼問題？ +

從較廣泛的客群或尚未確認的需求，收斂出一個主要目標客群，以及清楚的「我們如何能……」問題敘述。

工作主題
  • 盤點可能的目標客群
  • 找出各客群的重要痛點或尚未被滿足的期待
  • 選定主要目標客群
  • 建立主要的 How Might We 問題敘述
預期產出

主要目標客群、核心使用者需求、主要 HMW 問題敘述，以及第一次調整後的 Innovative Idea Summary。

E Empathize 同理理解使用者行為與需求 我們怎麼知道，這個問題對目標客群真的重要？ +

暫時放下對產品的預設，整理使用者的行為、需求、替代做法、想法與感受，建立同理心地圖。

工作主題
  • 設計不透露產品構想的問卷與訪談題目
  • 檢視具差異性的 AI 模擬使用者行為資料
  • 依「說、做、想、感受」整理證據
  • 保留行為模式與原始資料之間的連結
預期產出

使用者行為資料，以及可回溯資料來源的「說／做／想／感受」同理心地圖。

A Analyze 分析從證據找出機會 我們從使用者的痛點、期待與行為中，學到了什麼？ +

解讀反覆出現的行為模式，說明它為什麼重要，並找出品牌可以創造價值、但尚未預設功能解法的機會領域。

工作主題
  • 將行為模式轉化為洞察
  • 辨識痛點與期待成果
  • 找出資料中的一致與矛盾
  • 定義有資料依據的機會領域
預期產出

洞察、痛點與期待成果、資料中的一致與矛盾，以及機會領域。

R Refine 精煉形成 MVP 概念 回應重要需求的最小完整體驗是什麼？ +

把機會領域轉化為更小的設計挑戰，做出功能取捨，並用完整的使用者體驗描述 MVP。

工作主題
  • 建立拆解後的 How Might We 問題
  • 發想並排序可能的 MVP 功能
  • 選出最小但完整的核心功能組合
  • 調整第一人稱使用者旅程與成功指標
預期產出

MVP 核心功能組合、第一人稱使用者旅程、待驗證假設、成功指標，以及第二次調整後的 MVP Concept Summary。

當天會使用的核心概念這些都是實際工作的工具。工作坊會讓參與者直接在題目中使用，而不是把它們當成抽象理論來學。 +

How Might We

用「我們如何能……」提出不預設答案的問題，為多種可能解法保留空間。

同理心地圖

依「說、做、想、感受」整理使用者資料，同時保留背後的資料依據。

洞察

解釋某個行為模式為何出現，以及它可能對產品設計代表什麼。

機會領域

在決定具體功能之前，先指出品牌可以為使用者創造價值的方向。

MVP

能提供核心價值、也能協助驗證重要假設的最小完整產品體驗。

使用者旅程

用第一人稱呈現使用者如何接觸、使用並感受這套 MVP。

團隊會帶走什麼

一套更容易說明、檢視與驗證的產品概念。

第一次調整

完成第一次 pivot 後的 Innovative Idea Summary，依主要目標客群與核心 HMW 問題，重新聚焦產品設計。

第二次調整

完成第二次 pivot 後的 MVP Concept Summary，把使用者依據、機會、產品設計選擇與使用者旅程連結起來。

模擬官方網站

用具體形式呈現 MVP，支援團隊討論、蒐集回饋與後續測試。

關於模擬資料

工作坊使用 AI 模擬的使用者行為資料，在一天內演練完整的研究與設計流程。這些資料可協助團隊形成假設，但不能視為市場驗證。下一步仍需要透過真實目標使用者來檢驗產品概念。

ACE CREATIVE LEADERSHIP WORKSHOP · LEVEL 2: FORGER

LEVEL 2 WORKSHOP · AUGUST 11, 2026

From an innovative idea to a tangible MVP concept.

Level 2 continues the brand innovation your team developed in Level 1. In one working day, you will clarify the user and problem, examine user-behavior evidence, define a coherent MVP, and make the concept visible through a mock official website.

How Level 2 works View the run-down ↓
TUESDAY, AUGUST 11, 20269:30 AM–5:30 PMTAIPEI

MESSAGE FROM COACHES

A personal note from Chris and Joshua

Dear friends,

I would like to take a moment to look back on the Applied Creativity Engine Creative Leadership Workshop Level 1: Explorer, which we completed together on April 14, 2026.

At the heart of the workshop was one simple idea:

Creativity is remix.

Innovation does not always begin with inventing something entirely new. It often begins by recognizing the capabilities a brand already possesses, then recombining them with new industries, new contexts, and new user needs.

Each of the six teams selected a well-known brand and explored its core strengths across five dimensions: Technology, Design, Business Model, Customer Engagement, and Ecosystem. From there, the teams examined the brand’s personality, beliefs, and leadership direction to identify its unique brand DNA.

Using SCAMPER and AI as creative partners, each team then explored how those existing capabilities could cross over into new industries and opportunities. Through discussion, judgment, and synthesis, every team moved from a wide range of possibilities to one innovative idea that was both creative and meaningfully aligned with the brand.

The six concepts were:

  1. Team 1 reimagined On as a private sports salon combining premium design, performance, comfort, and exclusive member services.
  2. Team 2 transformed Picky into an extreme-environment nutrition and survival solutions provider.
  3. Team 3 combined Nike stability footwear, gait data, wearable technology, and gamified member challenges to help people walk more steadily and move better.
  4. Team 4 created MUJI Temple, a modern retreat experience designed to reduce choice and distraction, helping people return to a state of “just enough.”
  5. Team 5 extended In-N-Out’s simplicity, quality, and secret-menu culture into an experimental minimalist coffee concept.
  6. Team 6 created Alive with Patagonia, a system that turns apparel into a long-term record of movement, adventure, and life experiences.

Each team then documented its concept in an Innovative Idea Summary and created a first-person user journey, helping transform an abstract idea into a product story that others could understand and imagine.

That was the purpose of Level 1: Explorer:

From no idea to an innovative idea.

On August 11, 2026, we will move into the next stage of the journey: Level 2: Forger.

In Forger, the coaches will guide each team through Human-Centered Design, Design Sprint methods, and AI-enabled acceleration. The goal is to transform each innovative idea into a more tangible, focused, and testable Minimal Viable Product Concept.

Each team will also create a mock official website, presenting the concept as though it were already launched. This will help clarify the target user, core problem, value proposition, key features, and intended user experience.

Explorer helped us discover new possibilities.

Forger will help us shape those possibilities into something tangible, visible, and ready to be developed further.

We look forward to continuing the journey with all of you on August 11.

Chris and Joshua

LEVEL 2 AT A GLANCE

One idea in. One clearer MVP concept out.

The focus is not to create more ideas. It is to take the idea your team already has and make it more specific, more human-centered, and concrete enough to discuss and test.

01Input from Level 1

An innovative idea for your selected brand

Your team’s Innovative Idea Summary, including the intended audience, assumed need, initial concept, and User Journey.

This is the starting hypothesis—not a fixed answer.
02Working process

A focused human-centered design cycle

Use the DEAR process to define the problem, examine behavior, interpret evidence, and make clear product choices.

The work is rapid, team-based, and AI-assisted.
03Output from Level 2

A tangible MVP concept

A refined MVP Concept Summary with a primary audience, evidence-linked features, a User Journey, and a mock official website.

Concrete enough to review, share, and validate next.

ACE’s original DEAR process

Developed by Applied Creativity Engine, DEAR brings together human-centered design and design sprint practices. Four connected moves help teams turn an initial idea into an evidence-linked MVP.

D DefineFocus the audience and problem What problem are we solving—and for whom? +

Move from a broad audience or assumed need to one primary Target Audience and a clear How Might We problem statement.

Working topics
  • Identify possible Target Audience groups
  • Connect each group to a meaningful Pain Point or Unfulfilled Desire
  • Select the primary Target Audience
  • Frame the main How Might We problem statement
Output

Primary Target Audience, core user need, main HMW statement, and a revised Innovative Idea Summary after the first pivot.

E EmpathizeUnderstand behavior and needs How do we know this problem matters to the people we are designing for? +

Look beyond opinions and product assumptions. Organize behavior, needs, workarounds, thoughts, and emotions into an Empathy Map.

Working topics
  • Design concept-blind survey and interview questions
  • Review varied, AI-simulated User Behavior Data
  • Organize evidence into Say, Do, Think, and Feel
  • Retain links between patterns and source evidence
Output

User Behavior Data and an evidence-traceable Say / Do / Think / Feel Empathy Map.

A AnalyzeTurn evidence into opportunities What have we learned about users’ pains, desired outcomes, and behavior? +

Interpret recurring patterns, explain why they matter, and identify solution-neutral spaces where the innovation could create value.

Working topics
  • Convert behavior patterns into Insights
  • Identify Pains and desired Gains
  • Examine Alignments and Contradictions
  • Define evidence-backed Opportunity Areas
Output

Insights, Pains & Gains, Alignments & Contradictions, and Opportunity Areas.

R RefineShape the MVP concept What is the smallest coherent experience that addresses the strongest needs? +

Translate opportunity areas into smaller design challenges, make feature choices, and express the MVP as an end-to-end user experience.

Working topics
  • Create decomposed How Might We statements
  • Generate and prioritize possible MVP features
  • Select the minimum coherent feature set
  • Refine the first-person User Journey and success measures
Output

MVP feature set, first-person User Journey, assumptions, success measures, and a refined MVP Concept Summary after the second pivot.

Key concepts used during the dayThese are practical working tools. Participants will use them in context rather than study them as abstract theory. +

How Might We

A solution-neutral question that creates room for more than one possible answer.

Empathy Map

A way to organize what users say, do, think, and feel without losing the underlying evidence.

Insight

An explanation of why a behavior pattern may occur and what it could mean for the design.

Opportunity Area

A space where the brand could create value before deciding on a specific feature.

MVP

The smallest coherent product experience that delivers the central outcome and tests important assumptions.

User Journey

A first-person view of how someone encounters, uses, and experiences the proposed MVP.

WHAT YOUR TEAM LEAVES WITH

A concept that is easier to explain, review, and test.

First pivot

A revised Innovative Idea Summary that focuses the product design around one primary Target Audience and the main HMW problem.

Second pivot

A refined MVP Concept Summary connecting user evidence, opportunities, product design choices, and the User Journey.

Mock website

A tangible representation of the MVP that supports team discussion, feedback, and future testing.

A note on simulated data

AI-simulated User Behavior Data is used to rehearse the research and design workflow within one day. It helps teams form hypotheses; it does not count as market validation. The next step is to test the concept with real target users.
